checks: The weighted centroid is interior because the uniform component has positive volume on interior slabs. A closed containing cap can be tightened to pass through the centroid. The uniform cap tail decreases continuously and strictly across its projection interval, and its dth root is concave by Brunn–Minkowski applied to parallel caps. Under uniform volume the tail rank is uniform; the additional dominated measure pushes forward to a subdensity h in [0,1].

Jensen for the cap root under the normalized weighted measure gives the first inequality with uniform contribution d/(d+1). The nondecreasing rank test is minimized by filling the leftmost portions on [0,p] and [p,1] separately, using lengths e and a−e. Domination ensures those lengths are feasible even when either is zero or fills its interval.

Dividing by qp^q gives φ(U)+Lφ(Q)+Lφ(E)≥L/(d+1). The desired inequality is exactly D=U+LQ−L(k−1)E≤L(1+k). The three scalar Fenchel choices are 1/d, 1/d and −(k−1)/d with weights 1,L,L, so their affine terms sum to D/d. Rearrangement gives the stated sufficient inequality after multiplying by d(d+1).

After dividing by L, only the subtracted term (d+1)k/L changes on the right and the right side increases with L. At L=2, the exact left and right values are 0 and 2 in d=1 and 27/128 and 13/4 in d=2. For d≥3 use 2≤k<87/32<11/4 and (1−1/d)^(d−1)≤1/2; the two sides are strictly below and at least d, respectively.
